chapterNote: The Ascension psalm — the church has read it on Ascension Day since the early centuries, because its center is a King going UP: God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of the ram's horn. It is the shortest of the enthronement psalms and the loudest: clap your hands, all you peoples; shout to God with a ringing cry; sing praises, sing praises, sing praises, sing praises — the word comes five times in two verses. The reason is His rank: the LORD Most High is awesome, a great King over the whole earth, who subdues nations under Israel's feet and chose Jacob's inheritance out of love. Then the picture that made it a coronation hymn: God ascends His holy throne and reigns over the nations, and the nobles of the peoples come and gather as the people of Abraham's God — the Gentiles walking into the covenant, because every shield on earth belongs to Him. Israel sang it at the New Year with the shofar; the church sings it forty days after Easter, when the King who came down went up.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you peoples! Shout to God with a ringing cry of triumph!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] for the sons [ben] of Korah [Qorach]. O clap [taqa — strike, clap] your hands [kaph], all ye people [am]; shout [rua] unto God [Elohim] with the voice [qol] of triumph [rinnah — a ringing cry].
1.notes: kol-ha-ammim tiqu-khaph (H5971, H8628, H3709): ALL the peoples told to clap — the applause of a coronation, and the Gentiles are in the audience from the first line. hariu l-Elohim be-qol rinnah (H7321, H430, H6963, H7440): the war-shout of Jericho turned into the ringing cry of a feast.

2.text: For the LORD Most High is awesome — a great King over all the earth.
2.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] most high [Elyon] is terrible [yare — awesome, to be feared]; He is a great [gadol] King [melek] over all the earth [eretz].
2.notes: YHWH Elyon nora (H3068, H5945, H3372): the Most High, the title of Melchizedek's God, and nora — 'terrible' in the KJV's sense, the One who makes you catch your breath. melek gadol al-kol-ha-aretz (H4428, H1419, H776): not Israel's tribal deity but the earth's King.

3.text: He subdues peoples under us, and nations beneath our feet.
3.amp: He shall subdue [dabar — bring under, speak down] the people [am] under us, and the nations [leom] under our feet [regel].
3.notes: yadber ammim tachtenu (H1696, H5971): the verb is 'to speak' in its rarer sense of driving down — nations subdued as if by a word. u-leummim tachat raglenu (H3816, H7272): under our feet, the posture of Joshua 10:24 and Psalm 110:1.

4.text: He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loved. Selah.
4.amp: He shall choose [bachar] our inheritance [nachalah] for us, the excellency [gaon — pride, majesty] of Jacob [Yaaqob] whom He loved [ahab]. Selah [selah].
4.notes: yivchar-lanu et-nachalatenu (H977, H5159): the land as a chosen gift, not a conquest earned — geon Yaaqob (H1347, H3290), the pride of Jacob, the thing Jacob's sons could boast of; asher ahev (H157): whom He loved. Election's root is love (cf. Deuteronomy 7:7-8).

5.text: God has gone up with a shout of acclamation — the LORD, with the blast of the ram's horn.
5.amp: God [Elohim] is gone up [alah] with a shout [teruah — the blast, the acclamation], the LORD [YHWH] with the sound [qol] of a trumpet [shophar — ram's horn].
5.notes: alah Elohim bi-teruah (H5927, H430, H8643): God has ASCENDED — the ark going up to Zion with David's shouting (cf. 2 Samuel 6:15), the Ascension of Christ read here by the church (cf. Acts 1:9-11; Ephesians 4:8). YHWH be-qol shophar (H6963, H7782): the ram's horn that announced kings and the New Year.

6.text: Make music to God, make music! Make music to our King, make music!
6.amp: Sing praises [zamar] to God [Elohim], sing praises: sing praises unto our King [melek], sing praises.
6.notes: zammeru four times (H2167) in one verse — the psalm's drumbeat, and a fifth in verse 7. Elohim, then malkenu (H430, H4428): God, and OUR King — the ascended One is not a distant monarch but the one Israel calls its own.

7.text: For God is King of all the earth; sing praises with a well-taught song.
7.amp: For God [Elohim] is the King [melek] of all the earth [eretz]: sing ye praises [zamar] with understanding ['every one that hath understanding', maskil, the KJV margin — a skillful, insightful song].
7.notes: ki melekh kol-ha-aretz Elohim (H4428, H776, H430): the claim of verse 2 repeated as the ground of the fifth zammeru (H2167). zammeru maskil (H7919): sing a maskil — the Psalter's word for a psalm of skill and insight (Psalms 32, 42, 142). Praise with the mind engaged, not only the lungs (cf. 1 Corinthians 14:15).

8.text: God reigns over the nations; God has taken His seat on His holy throne.
8.amp: God [Elohim] reigns [malak] over the heathen [goy]: God sits [yashab] upon the throne [kisse] of His holiness [qodesh].
8.notes: malakh Elohim al-goyim (H4427, H430, H1471): God is KING over the nations — the enthronement formula of Psalms 93, 96-99. Elohim yashav al-kisse qodsho (H3427, H3678, H6944): seated, the ascent of verse 5 completed. Hebrews 1:3 — 'sat down at the right hand of the Majesty' — is this verse fulfilled.

9.text: The nobles of the peoples have gathered as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God. He is lifted very high.
9.amp: The princes [nadib — nobles, the willing] of the people [am] are gathered together [asaph], even the people of the God [Elohim] of Abraham [Abraham]: for the shields [magen] of the earth [eretz] belong unto God; He is greatly [meod] exalted [alah].
9.notes: nedibe ammim neesaphu (H5081, H5971, H622): the nobles of the PEOPLES — Gentiles — gathered as am Elohe Abraham (H430, H85), the people of Abraham's God: Genesis 12:3's 'all families of the earth' arriving. magine-eretz (H4043, H776), the earth's shields — its rulers and protectors — are God's property; meod naalah (H3966, H5927): the verb of verse 5, once more. He went up; He is very high.
